yesterday.note: LIVE read, date range Yesterday (Sep 10, 2026). SEP 9 WAS THE WORST DAY ON RECORD AND SEP 10 IS WORSE. Spend $76.07 is up another $15.24 (+25%) on top of Sep 9's $60.83, and average CPC rose again to $4.00 from $3.04 -- that is a third consecutive daily increase and more than triple the $1.17 CPC of Sep 8. Volume did not follow the money: 744 impressions (+62) and 19 clicks (-1). Two days ago this account bought a click for roughly a dollar; yesterday it paid four. SPEND BREACHED THE ACCOUNT BUDGET FOR THE SECOND DAY RUNNING AND BY A WIDER MARGIN. The account daily budget is $40.00; Sep 10 spent $76.07 -- 90% over, against 52% over on Sep 9. Brewhouse Lunch took $50.00 on a $25.00/day budget (exactly 2x) for 518 impressions and 10 clicks at a $5.00 CPC. Brewhouse Dinner took $26.07 on $15.00/day for 226 impressions and 9 clicks at a $2.90 CPC and a 3.98% CTR -- the healthier of the two. Two days at roughly 1.7x the daily cap will empty a monthly budget well before month end. CONVERSIONS READ 0.00 and are still flagged as calculating; an in-product banner separately credits Brewhouse Dinner with a 200% week-on-week increase in clicks. Neither figure is reliable at this reporting lag. THE STRUCTURAL FLAG IS UNCHANGED AND THIS IS NOW ITS THIRD RUN AS PRIME SUSPECT: both live Search campaigns read 'Eligible (Limited) -- All ads limited by policy'. A policy-limited account competing for a shrinking slice of inventory is exactly what a CPC that quadruples in three days looks like. The policy manager pass is overdue. Account budget $40.00/day; 2 live campaigns, 4 paused, 2 drafts in progress.

yelpAds.lastUpdated: 2026-09-11T14:45:00Z -- LIVE, biz.yelp.com opened successfully and both the Ad performance and Ad settings panels rendered in full.

billingPeriod.note: LIVE. $142.81 across the first 10 days of the September billing period = $14.28/day against a $13/day average budget, about 10% over. The trend reversed this run: the per-day average had fallen from $15.91 (Sep 5 read) to $14.33 (Sep 8) to $13.37 (Sep 8 billing read), and has now ticked back up. Sep 9 and Sep 10 together spent $35.88, roughly $17.94/day -- well above the $13 target. Delivery is clearly not stalled any more; if anything Yelp is now spending ahead of budget while the estimated audience size still reads Limited.

yelpAds.audienceSizeNote: STILL LIMITED -- SECOND CONSECUTIVE RUN, AND NOW CONFIRMED RATHER THAN INFERRED. The Ad settings panel rendered completely this run and Estimated audience size reads 'Limited' with Yelp's own explanation: 'Control features can limit how often your ad shows and lead to a higher cost-per-click.' The likely controls are the 12 manual keywords and the 5-mile radius. This is the single most actionable Yelp item and it has now persisted for two days. Widening the radius or letting Yelp select keywords would move it back toward Ideal. Note the cost-per-click did rise this run, from $1.20 to $1.30, exactly as the warning predicts -- though at $1.30 Yelp is still buying clicks at roughly a third of what Google Ads paid yesterday ($4.00).

yelpAds.bonusBudgetNote: CONFIRMED ABSENT, AND THIS TIME ON A CLEAN READ. The Ad settings 'All settings' panel rendered completely this run -- keywords, budget, location, design, audience size and ad preview all present -- and there is no bonus-budget line anywhere on it. Previous runs could not distinguish 'absent' from 'failed to render'. This run can: there is no active bonus budget on this account.
yelpAds.yelpListingNote: Yelp ad preview shows The Brewhouse at 775 Yelp reviews, American/Seafood/Brewpubs, 229 W Montecito St, $$, 'Locally owned & operated, Established in 1998'.
yelpAds.note: PERFORMANCE MOVED SLIGHTLY THE WRONG WAY ON EVERY HEADLINE. Versus the Sep 9 read: ad impressions 28.9k (was 29.7k), page visits from ads 362 (was 383), leads from ads 102 (was 105), cost-per-click $1.30 (was $1.20), cost-per-lead $3.76 (was $3.34). The share figures slipped too -- ads now drive 51% of page visits, down from 54%. None of these moves is large on its own and 30-day windows roll off good days, but the direction is consistent and it matches the Limited audience-size warning. CONTEXT WORTH KEEPING IN VIEW: Yelp delivered 102 leads in 30 days at $3.76 each. Google Ads spent $76.07 in a single day for 19 clicks and zero recorded conversions. Whatever is wrong with the Google account, Yelp remains the efficient channel by a wide margin.
